newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mostly sink with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mostly sink with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly crumbled on Friday in sluggish trade, undermined by a sinking crude market and bearish East Coast weather forecasts, industry sources said.
"No one needs oil right now. There's no demand and gas is still much cheaper," said an East Coast utility source, noting a number of eastern utilities have made the switch to gas.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent skidded more than 50 cents to $15.50-75 a barrel, while March one percent paper, which was quoted early at $15.50, sank later to the low-$15s on weaker crude, down 75 cents on the day, traders said.
NYH high sulphurs also lost serious ground, with 2.2 sinking about $1 to $13.75-14.00 amid little HS interest and good avails, traders said.

NYH 0.3 percent low pour and high pour again notionally were steady at $19.25 and $17.25-50, respectively, but fairly cheap eastern city gate gas prices were expected to keep HP on the defensive near-term.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent slipped a quarter to $14.50-75, while three percent was down slightly at about $12.
One trader said a fairly prompt USG two percent cargo sold at $11.75 but the deal was not confirmed.

New York city gate gas prices fell by about five cents to $2.10/mmBtu, or about $13.23 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, held relatively steady at about $1.80/mmBtu, or $11.34 a barrel equivalent.
